Southern Chicken and Dumplings

Jump to Recipe
By Rosie Alexander Updated: September 23, 2026 Leave a Comment
This post may contain affiliate links.

A cozy pot of Southern chicken and dumplings — juicy chicken simmered in a velvety broth, topped off with fluffy dumplings made from scratch, no shortcuts.

Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 8:50
Instaread

Y’all, if there’s one pot on the stove that means somebody in my family is having a rough week, needs a little comfort, or we’re just plain celebrating — it’s this one. Chicken and dumplings has been a staple in Southern kitchens for generations, and once you make it from scratch, you’ll understand why. Tender chicken, a rich savory broth loaded with vegetables, and soft, pillowy dumplings dropped right in to finish cooking in all that flavor. No canned biscuits, no shortcuts — just real ingredients, cousins.

This one takes a little time, but I promise you every minute is worth it. Let’s get into it.

Why You’ll Love This Chicken and Dumplings Recipe

This isn’t a thrown-together weeknight dinner — it’s a low-and-slow, one-pot meal that fills the whole house with that smell that makes everybody wander into the kitchen asking “what’s cooking?” A few reasons this recipe is a keeper:

The chicken gets browned first, which builds a deeper flavor into the broth than just boiling it straight. The vegetables — onion, bell peppers, carrots, and celery — cook right in the pot so every bite of broth carries their flavor. And the dumplings are made from scratch with self-rising flour, so they come out soft and fluffy rather than dense.

Ingredients You’ll Need

For the chicken:

  • 4-6 lb whole chicken: cut into pieces
  • 3 teaspoons poultry seasoning
  • 3 teaspoons seasoning salt
  • 1 teaspoon black pepper
  • 2 teaspoons garlic powder
  • 2 teaspoons onion powder
  • 3 tablespoons vegetable oil

The stew:

  • 32 oz chicken broth
  • 3 bay leaves
  • 2 sprigs fresh thyme
  • 1 large yellow onion, diced
  • 4 cloves garlic
  • 1 medium red bell pepper, diced
  • 1 medium green bell pepper, diced
  • 5 large carrots, diced
  • 5 celery stalks, diced
  • 1 teaspoon parsley flakes
  • half & half
  • salt and pepper to taste

For the dumplings:

  • 1 1/2 cups self-rising flour
  • 1/2 teaspoon parsley flakes (optional)
  • 1/2 cup half & half
  • 3 tablespoons salted butter, melted
  • 1/2 tsp salt

A note on ingredients: self-rising flour already has leavening and salt built in, so it’s what gives these dumplings their soft, fluffy texture without needing baking powder. If you only have all-purpose flour on hand, whisk in 2 1/4 teaspoons baking powder and 3/4 teaspoon salt per cup.

How to Make Chicken and Dumplings From Scratch

Season and brown the chicken: Rinse the chicken and remove everything from the cavity, then cut it into pieces. Season with the poultry seasoning, seasoning salt, black pepper, garlic powder, and onion powder. Heat the vegetable oil in a heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat, and once it’s hot, brown the chicken in batches on each side. Remove and set aside — you’re not cooking it through yet, just building flavor.

Build the stew: Add the diced onion and bell peppers to the same pot and cook until translucent. Return the chicken to the pot along with the garlic, carrots, and celery. Pour in the chicken broth, then add the bay leaves and fresh thyme. Stir, cover, reduce the heat to medium, and let it cook for 35 minutes.

Shred the chicken and enrich the broth:Remove the lid and take the chicken out, placing it in a large bowl. Once it’s cool enough to handle, remove the skin and bones and set the meat aside. Stir the half & half into the pot until well combined, then return the chicken to the pot. Cover and cook another 15 minutes.

Make the dumplings: While the stew finishes, sift the self-rising flour into a mixing bowl and stir in the salt and parsley flakes. Pour in the half & half and melted butter, then use a fork to combine everything into a sticky dough.

Drop the dumplings and finish: Uncover the pot and drop spoonfuls of the dumpling dough right into the simmering stew. Cover and cook for 10 minutes, then uncover, gently stir, remove from the heat, serve hot, and enjoy.

Tips for the Best Chicken and Dumplings

Don’t skip browning the chicken — that step alone makes the broth taste like it’s been on the stove all day. Keep the lid on while the dumplings cook; lifting it too soon lets steam escape and can leave them dense instead of fluffy. And resist stirring too hard once the dumplings go in — a gentle stir keeps them from breaking apart into the broth.

If your broth needs a little more body at the end, you can mash a few of the softened dumplings against the side of the pot to naturally thicken it, or stir in a small cornstarch slurry.

Storage and Reheating

Chicken and dumplings are kept in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 3 days. Reheat gently on the stovetop over low heat, adding a splash of broth or water since the dumplings soak up liquid as they sit. Freezing is best done before the dumplings go in, since they can get a little mushy after thawing — freeze the chicken and broth mixture for up to 3 months, then make a fresh batch of dumplings when you’re ready to serve.

Frequently Asked Questions

What’s the difference between drop dumplings and rolled dumplings?

Drop dumplings, like the ones in this recipe, are spoonfuls of soft dough dropped straight into the pot, giving you fluffy, biscuit-like bites. Rolled dumplings are rolled thin and cut into strips, cooking up flatter and more noodle-like. Both are Southern classics — this recipe leans toward the fluffier drop-style.

Can I use rotisserie chicken instead?

You can, though you’ll lose some of the depth that browning a whole chicken adds to the broth. If you’re short on time, shred a rotisserie chicken and add it in after building the vegetable and broth base, skipping the browning step.

Can I make this ahead of time?

The stew base can be made a day ahead and refrigerated. Bring it back to a simmer, then make your dumpling dough fresh and drop it in right before serving.

Why did my dumplings turn out gummy?

When the dumplings turn out gummy, this usually means the pot wasn’t covered while they cooked, or they cooked too long uncovered — the steam is what cooks them through and keeps them light.

Southern Chicken and Dumplings Recipe

Southern chicken and dumplings recipe — tender chicken, a rich creamy broth, and soft homemade dumplings made completely from scratch.
Print Recipe Pin Recipe
Course Main Course
Keyword homemade, southern,
Prep Time 20 minutes minutes
Cook Time 1 hour hour 10 minutes minutes
Servings 8 people
Calories 496kcal

Ingredients

For the chicken

  • 4-6 lb whole chicken cut into pieces
  • 3 tsp poultry seasoning
  • 3 tsp seasoning salt
  • 1 tsp black pepper
  • 2 tsp garlic powder
  • 2 tsp onion powder
  • 3 tbsp vegetable oil

For the stew

  • 32 oz chicken broth
  • 3 bay leaves
  • 2 sprigs fresh thyme
  • 1 large yellow onion diced
  • 4 cloves garlic whole
  • 1 medium red bell pepper diced
  • 1 medium green bell pepper diced
  • 5 large carrots diced
  • 5 celery stalks diced
  • 1 tsp parsley flakes
  • 1/2 cup half & half
  • Salt and pepper to taste

For the dumplings

  • 1 1/2 cups self-rising flour
  • 1/2 tsp parsley flakes optional
  • 1/2 cup half & half
  • 3 tbsp salted butter melted
  • 1/2 tsp salt

Instructions

  • Remove everything from the cavity. Cut into pieces.
  • Season the chicken pieces with the poultry seasoning, seasoning salt, black pepper, garlic powder, and onion powder.
  • Heat the vegetable oil in a heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
  • Once hot, brown the chicken in batches on each side. Remove and set aside.
  • Add the diced onion and bell peppers to the pot; cook until translucent.
  • Add the chicken back to the pot along with the garlic, carrots, and celery.
  • Pour in the chicken broth and add the bay leaves and fresh thyme.
  • Stir everything together, cover, and reduce heat to medium. Cook 35 minutes.
  • Remove the lid and take the chicken out of the pot; place it in a large bowl.
  • Remove the skin and bones from the chicken; set the meat aside.
  • Return to the pot and stir in the half & half until well combined. Add the chicken back in.
  • Cover and cook 15 minutes.
  • Meanwhile, sift the self-rising flour into a mixing bowl. Stir in the salt and parsley flakes.
  • Pour in the half & half and melted butter.
  • Use a fork to combine until it forms a sticky dough.
  • Uncover the pot and drop spoonfuls of the dough in. Cover and cook 10 minutes.
  • Serve and enjoy!

Notes

Self-rising flour already has leavening and salt built in, so it’s what gives these dumplings their soft, fluffy texture without needing baking powder. If you only have all-purpose flour on hand, whisk in 2 1/4 teaspoons baking powder and 3/4 teaspoon salt per cup.
